business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Skyways Air Services Limited and its subsidiaries provide air freight forwarding, ocean freight forwarding, technology-driven express cargo and parcel delivery, trucking, warehousing, customs broking and value-added logistics services to exporters, importers and other freight forwarders across domestic and international markets. The company owns no aircraft or shipping lines and buys capacity from third-party carriers on a back-to-back basis after customer confirmation, acting as a consolidator that aggregates smaller shipments into competitive-rate loads. Its technology subsidiary sGate Tech Solutions builds the proprietary booking, tracking and workflow platforms (SLS HIKE, SLS 100X, SLS 100X 2.0, Cargo Dash, Skart-Edge and the pre-launch ASAP) that run these operations.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company describes a deliberate backward-and-forward integration strategy executed through subsidiaries rather than owned transport assets. Stated verbatim in Our Business: 'In response to the evolving dynamics and increasing competitiveness of the global freight forwarding industry, our company adopted a proactive strategy aimed at enhancing operational efficiency, broadening market access, and delivering comprehensive, integrated logistics solutions to our customers through a combination of backward and forward integration. To support this strategic vision, our company incorporated and acquired multiple subsidiary entities, both within India and across key international markets.' In Business Strategies: 'As a comprehensive logistics solutions provider, we strategically leverage both backward and forward integration to optimize cost efficiencies and streamline service delivery across the supply chain. By internalizing critical functions such as last-mile delivery and customer support, we significantly reduce reliance on external courier services and call centre providers, thereby eliminating associated fees while ensuring a consistently high standard of service reliability and responsiveness. This end-to-end control over upstream procurement and downstream distribution operations enables us to retain greater revenue within the organization...' The group comprises 17 Indian subsidiaries, 6 foreign subsidiaries and 6 step-down subsidiaries, each with a specific mandate: warehousing (Skyways SLS Logistik Pvt Ltd), road transportation (Phantom Road Express Pvt Ltd), technology platforms (sGate Tech Solutions Pvt Ltd 51%, SLS ASAP Tech Systems Pvt Ltd), LCL ocean consolidation (Hubload SLS Services Pvt Ltd), tech-driven express door-to-door cargo and courier (Skart Global Express Pvt Ltd 95%), logistics skill development (SLS Logistik Academy Pvt Ltd 90%), e-commerce retail and digital marketing (SLS Retail Supermart Pvt Ltd 90%), ocean and warehousing (Forin Container Line Pvt Ltd 82.27%), cross-border freight forwarding (Surgeport Logistics Pvt Ltd 76%, Brace Port Logistics Ltd 51.09%), and specialised pharma/automotive ocean and air logistics (Odyssey Logistics Pvt Ltd 51%), plus international freight forwarding subsidiaries in Germany, Hong Kong, Dubai, Vietnam, Cambodia, the UK, the UAE, the USA, Canada and Saudi Arabia. Upstream, the model remains asset-light and carrier-dependent: 'We rely extensively on third-party carriers for the transportation of cargo, as we do not operate our own aircraft or shipping lines. Consequently, our business is 100% dependent on the availability, pricing, and service quality of such carriers.' Forward integration into infrastructure is proposed but not yet operational - the Company has undertaken a strategic initiative to expand into management and maintenance of cargo terminals (air and ocean), CFS, ICDs, logistics parks, industrial parks, warehousing complexes, cold storage facilities, freight corridors and dry ports, and has bid jointly with Swissport International AG for a DBFOT cargo terminal at Kolkata airport.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Dependence on trade volumes and economic conditions - demand tracks the movement of goods, and any slowdown in industrial output, consumer demand or GDP growth reduces cargo volumes; tariffs, sanctions and geopolitical events can disrupt routes and delay shipments
- Seasonality - festivals, inventory cycles and export deadlines make volumes and operating performance vary quarter to quarter
- Fuel price volatility - ATF, diesel and marine fuel costs flow through from airlines, shipping lines and road operators; surcharges lag price rises, and pass-through may be incomplete under contractual and competitive pressure, compressing margins
- Thin, buy-sell spread economics - cost of services was Rs 2,50,690.56 lakhs against revenue from operations of Rs 2,81,289.89 lakhs in FY26, so EBITDA margin sits at 4.47% (FY25 3.85%, FY24 3.75%) and PAT margin at 2.26%; small rate movements move profit disproportionately
- Mix shift toward pharmaceuticals - pharma rose to 22.89% of FY26 revenue from 9.11% in FY25, while spare parts fell from 9.82% to 4.37%; realisation per air tonne fell to Rs 2.58 lakhs from Rs 2.80 lakhs and per ocean TEU to Rs 1.49 lakhs from Rs 1.84 lakhs even as volumes rose
- Working capital cycle funded by borrowings - the working capital gap was Rs 31,107.09 lakhs in FY26 (FY25 Rs 23,705.89 lakhs), financed 86.23% by working capital loans; trade receivables of Rs 57,947.65 lakhs at FY26-end; receivable holding period 64 days, payable holding 50 days
- Cash conversion has lagged profit - CFO was Rs 11,361.60 lakhs in FY26 but only Rs 201.05 lakhs in FY25 against PAT of Rs 4,813.97 lakhs, and negative Rs 904.17 lakhs in FY24 against PAT of Rs 3,449.35 lakhs
- Rising finance cost - Rs 4,807.64 lakhs in FY26 against Rs 2,881.38 lakhs in FY25 and Rs 1,877.40 lakhs in FY24; debt-to-equity 1.26 (FY26), 1.42 (FY25), 1.92 (FY24); credit ratings CRISIL A/Stable, CARE A/Stable and CARE A1
- Minority leakage - profit attributable to non-controlling interests rose to Rs 2,251.50 lakhs in FY26 from Rs 897.11 lakhs in FY25, so EPS fell to Rs 3.56 from Rs 3.71 even though consolidated PAT grew, and RoNW on parent figures fell to 12.33% from 15.85%
- Supplier concentration on the cost side - top 5 suppliers were 36.01% and top 10 were 49.00% of FY26 cost of service
- Retention of experienced management and qualified workforce - attrition raises compensation cost and reduces operational efficiency; consolidated employee base 1,193 in FY26

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Keep growing and strengthening the scope of current operations through cost efficiency - process efficiency, workforce optimisation, value analysis, and backward/forward integration that internalises last-mile delivery and customer support to cut third-party courier and call-centre fees
- Increase the development of infrastructure - augment capacity to handle higher freight volumes and a wider range of cargo types, add hubs, and advance automation
- Strengthen and enhance customer connections - grow wallet share with existing clients and penetrate new industry sectors, and introduce traditional non-express freight, domestic air cargo, urban last-mile distribution and temperature-controlled logistics
- Improve technological abilities - complete SLS 100X 2.0 (in advanced stages of development) and commercially roll out ASAP (Any Shipping Any Place), a single digital interface for multi-modal rate discovery, booking and shipment management, currently in pre-launch
- Venture into rapidly developing global markets - partner with local logistics providers, customs brokers and government agencies; establish regional hubs in high-growth areas such as Southeast Asia or the Middle East; and create urban micro-hubs for last-mile e-commerce delivery
- Diversify the service portfolio into asset-linked logistics infrastructure - development, management, operation and maintenance of air and ocean cargo terminals, CFS, ICDs, logistics parks, warehousing and allied facilities

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The stated expansion is a move from a pure asset-light forwarder into asset-linked logistics infrastructure, plus deeper geographic and warehouse capacity. On the infrastructure leg, the Company has entered a consortium with Swissport International AG and jointly bid for the tender invited by AAI Cargo Logistics and Allied Services Company Ltd to develop a new cargo terminal at Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata, on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer basis; the financial bid was scheduled to open on February 12, 2026 and the bid validity has been extended to August 14, 2026, so the outcome is not known as at the RHP date. It is also empanelled as Custom House Agent for exhibition cargo at Bharat Mandapam (ITPO), New Delhi. On warehousing, the group ran 5 warehouses at FY26-end (2 of the Company, 2 of Odyssey Logistics, 1 of RIV Worldwide UK) against 3 at FY24-end, and material subsidiary Forin Container Line is constructing an Okhla (New Delhi) warehouse funded by a Rs 1,200.00 lakh term loan, which the RHP says "will be operational by August 2026". Geographically, presence rose from 10 countries in FY25 to 12 in FY26 (India plus Thailand, Bangladesh, UK, Saudi Arabia, Cambodia, Vietnam, Hong Kong, UAE, USA, Canada, Germany), with 28 cities across 12 Indian states/UTs, and the strategy is to add regional hubs in Southeast Asia or the Middle East and urban micro-hubs for last-mile delivery. Express-cargo reach grew to 1,204 pin codes and 31 PUD centres in FY26 from 1,006 and 19 in FY24. Growth to date has been substantially inorganic - Rs 8,476.50 lakhs, Rs 7,053.01 lakhs and Rs 3,468.43 lakhs of net cash went to acquisition of subsidiaries in FY26, FY25 and FY24, and goodwill stands at Rs 9,865.95 lakhs. There is no manufacturing capacity expansion; the Company does not own aircraft or ships and buys carrier capacity back-to-back.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Experienced promoters: Mr. Yashpal Sharma and Mr. Tarun Sharma, with cumulative experience of more than two decades in logistics; Yashpal Sharma has over 30 years of experience and was President of Air Cargo Forum India in 2022-24
- Claimed No. 1 rank as an Indian "Air Freight Forwarder" by AWBs generated, per World ACD Market Data, for four consecutive calendar years 2022-2025
- Comprehensive single-window range of logistics solutions - air, ocean, express parcel, trucking, customs clearance, warehousing, inventory management and supply chain software - reducing dependence on any single service line
- Broad partner network: performance-based agreements with major carriers, relationships with 56 airlines, and membership of six global forwarder networks said to encompass over 26,300 partners, extending international reach without fixed infrastructure cost
- Consolidator model - aggregating volumes from smaller forwarders, sub-agents and logistics firms into significant shipment loads to secure freight rates individual operators could not obtain
- Diverse and low-concentration customer base: top 5 customers were 14.04% and top 10 were 20.69% of FY26 revenue from operations; 9,504 customers and 65 key industries served in FY26
- In-house technology: proprietary platforms built by a 51%-owned technology subsidiary, with SLS 100X carrying 5,587 registered users, direct Qatar Airways integration, and OCR/RPA/machine-learning automation of data capture
- Long-standing client relationships, several dating from 2010-2018, supporting repeat business; and accreditations (IATA, AEO-LO, WHO-GDP, C-TPAT, ISO 9001/14001/45001) that underpin regulated cargo such as pharmaceuticals

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Total dependence on third-party carriers - the Company owns no aircraft or shipping lines and its "business is 100% dependent on the availability, pricing, and service quality of such carriers" — Air cargo alone was 77.02% of FY26 revenue and air, ocean and express together 97.83%. Capacity is not chartered; space is secured back-to-back after customer confirmation, so any capacity withdrawal, rate spike or service disruption hits revenue directly and cannot be absorbed internally.
- Criminal FIR and consequent suspension of the AEO-LO certificate — FIR No. 0172 of 2025 (EOW Delhi, December 12, 2025) names the Company as Accused No. 3 and subsidiary Brace Port Logistics as Accused No. 2 on allegations of inflated freight invoicing and bribery; the complainant alleges business exceeding Rs 8,000 lakhs and direct loss of not less than Rs 4,420 lakhs. Following the FIR, CBIC suspended the Company's AEO-LO status with effect from May 4, 2026 and has issued a notice for revocation; during suspension the Company cannot avail AEO benefits. This is an operating-licence risk, not merely a legal-provision risk.
- Working-capital intensity funded almost entirely by borrowings — The working capital gap was Rs 31,107.09 lakhs (FY26), Rs 23,705.89 lakhs (FY25) and Rs 24,265.23 lakhs (FY24), financed 86.23%, 100.00% and 82.62% by working capital loans. The Company projects the requirement rising to Rs 56,300.54 lakhs in FY27 and Rs 68,536.98 lakhs in FY28 - an 80.99% jump in one year - and expects to keep relying on borrowings.
- Receivables risk and a history of weak or negative operating cash flow — Trade receivables were Rs 57,947.65 lakhs at FY26-end against revenue from operations of Rs 2,81,289.89 lakhs. CFO was only Rs 201.05 lakhs in FY25 against PAT of Rs 4,813.97 lakhs and negative Rs 904.17 lakhs in FY24. Receivables over 6 months old grew from Rs 204.32 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 1,637.47 lakhs (FY26) in the 6-months-to-1-year bucket alone.
- Supplier (carrier) concentration on the cost side — Top 5 suppliers accounted for 36.01%, 31.20% and 38.29% of cost of service in FY26, FY25 and FY24, and top 10 for 49.00%, 46.93% and 54.31%. There are limited air carriers in the market; loss of favourable terms with any of them directly compresses an already thin 4.47% EBITDA margin.
- Large and growing non-controlling interests dilute what reaches the listed shareholder — Only 12 of 29 group entities are wholly owned. Profit attributable to NCI rose to Rs 2,251.50 lakhs in FY26 from Rs 897.11 lakhs in FY25, so basic EPS fell to Rs 3.56 from Rs 3.71 even as consolidated PAT rose 32%. NCI equity is Rs 16,209.31 lakhs of total equity of Rs 49,473.52 lakhs.
- Acquisition-led growth and integration/goodwill risk — Growth has come substantially from buying stakes in other forwarders - net cash outflow on subsidiary acquisitions of Rs 8,476.50 lakhs, Rs 7,053.01 lakhs and Rs 3,468.43 lakhs in FY26/FY25/FY24 - leaving goodwill of Rs 9,865.95 lakhs. The RHP flags that anticipated benefits of recent acquisitions may not be fully realised, and several subsidiaries carry their own tax and regulatory proceedings (29 tax cases, Rs 640.72 lakhs).
- Contingent liabilities and commitments of Rs 28,908.02 lakhs at March 31, 2026, equal to 86.90% of net worth of Rs 33,264.21 lakhs — These are not provided for. Alongside them, indirect-tax disputes of Rs 3,650.35 lakhs have been decided against the Company at appellate level and are under appeal before the Tribunal, with Rs 422.72 lakhs already pre-deposited.
